stories.title: Gaza ceasefire turns one, but the killing goes on
stories.body: One year after the Gaza ceasefire took effect, Gaza's Health Ministry says 1,493 people have been killed and 5,299 wounded since the truce began. More than 100 aid and rights groups say the ceasefire exists in name only. Aid trucks are entering at about a third of the agreed rate, and no international stabilisation force has deployed. Israel now controls nearly two-thirds of the Strip, more than the roughly 50 percent agreed.
stories.why: Nigeria backs a two-state solution, and the ceasefire's anniversary is a likely current-affairs question.

cards.front: About how much of Gaza did Israel control one year into the ceasefire (October 2026)?
cards.back: Nearly two-thirds, more than the roughly 50 percent agreed.

stories.title: Iran targets the oil 'shuttle' out of Hormuz
stories.body: Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Iran will target a US-assisted shuttle that moves Gulf oil out through routes near Oman, and warned that US-linked facilities in the UAE could also be hit. Several tankers were damaged over the weekend, and at least 15 ships had been targeted in October. Only about 31 ships a day crossed the strait in late September, against 138 before the war. Iran says the US has accepted some of its conditions but insists on all of them before a deal.
stories.why: Shipping costs for Gulf crude have jumped to 25–30 percent of its price, which keeps world fuel prices high for importers like Nigeria.

cards.front: How many ships a day crossed the Strait of Hormuz before the 2026 war, and in late September 2026?
cards.back: About 138 before the war; about 31 in late September 2026.

stories.title: Military: 36 terrorists killed, 50 hostages freed in a week
stories.body: Defence Headquarters said troops killed 36 terrorists and rescued at least 50 kidnapped people between 2 and 8 October. In Borno, Operation Hadin Kai repelled an ISWAP assault on Kukawa. In Kebbi, Operation Fansan Yamma killed 10 Lakurawa fighters. In Imo, troops freed 20 prospective NYSC corps members abducted on the Owerri–Onitsha Expressway. The Chief of Defence Staff, General Olufemi Oluyede, urged citizens to report terrorist collaborators.
stories.why: It shows Nigeria's security threats in every zone at once, from ISWAP in the North-east to kidnapping in the South-east.

cards.front: Which military operation covers Kebbi and the North-west against Lakurawa and bandits?

stories.title: Trump: no strike on Iran before the midterms
stories.body: President Trump said the US will not attack Iran before the 3 November midterm elections, describing talks as productive. Vice-President JD Vance said Iran must make a meaningful cut to its uranium enrichment capacity, which experts see as softer than the earlier demand to end enrichment completely. Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran would answer the US response to its seven-day Hormuz plan within days. Iranian media reported explosions in the southern Strait, possibly from sea mines.
stories.why: Oil prices swing on every signal from Washington and Tehran, which feeds straight into Nigeria's fuel and budget planning.

cards.front: What did US Vice-President Vance demand of Iran in October 2026?
cards.back: A meaningful cut to its uranium enrichment capacity (Iran has reached 60% enrichment).

stories.title: Ukraine ready for three-way talks by end of October
stories.body: President Zelenskyy said Ukraine is ready for US-backed talks with Russia before the end of October, possibly in the United Arab Emirates. He spoke during a visit to Kyiv by German Chancellor Friedrich Merz. Moscow has also said it is open to October talks. Both sides are stepping up strikes on energy and transport as winter approaches.
stories.why: Any deal or escalation moves world wheat, fertiliser and fuel prices, which feed Nigerian inflation.

cards.front: Where are US–Ukraine–Russia talks proposed for October 2026?
cards.back: The United Arab Emirates (or another US-proposed venue).
